decisions.reason: Resizing the main board does not change the established three-board architecture or the roles and exclusions of its boards.
The new main-board dimensions require rearrangement but do not change the existing connector-edge, alignment, accessibility, or cable-routing constraints.
The 70×50 dimensions apply to the main board and do not alter the power board's mechanical form factor.
The same message's ESP32 edge-placement constraint is already fully represented by the candidate's existing message-543 INTRODUCE Event.
Changing the board outline does not alter which ESP32 pins require breakout holes or the permitted placement of those holes.
The reference to clean routing on four layers concerns the resized main board and does not modify the power board's layer stack or grounding strategy.
Retaining separate JST connectors is consistent with the existing separate power-and-signal connector design and does not change the established interboard signal connector specifications or pinouts.
The board resize and connector-modularity discussion do not change the panel reset connector, electrical action, or mounting implementation.
The source retains separate connectors and leaves the interboard power connector, topology, distribution, and pin-order rules unchanged.
The main-board outline change does not alter the charge-status LED path, connector, resistor, or population requirements.
The physical main-board resize does not change DCDC1 voltage regulation, current capacity, or Schottky-drop compensation.
The source does not change the panel power button's connector, main-board location, PWRON connection, or switch behavior.
